chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Rib'i ibn 'Abd Allah, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

“'Umar ibn al-Khattab gathered the companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said: What do you say about a man who comes to his wife and has intercourse with her but does not ejaculate? The Ansar said: Water is only from water. And the Muhajirun said: When the two circumcised parts meet, ghusl becomes obligatory upon him.

Then 'Umar said to 'Ali عليه السلام: What do you say, O Abu al-Hasan? So 'Ali عليه السلام said: “Do you impose upon him the hadd and stoning, yet do not impose upon him a sa' of water? When the two circumcised parts meet, ghusl has become obligatory upon him.” So 'Umar said: The correct statement is what the Muhajirun said, and leave what the Ansar said.”

key_terms.صَاعًا مِنْ مَاءٍ: a measure of water, here referring to the water used for ghusl
key_terms.يُخَالِطُهَا: he has intimate contact or intercourse with her
key_terms.ٱلرَّجْمَ: stoning as a legal penalty in the relevant case
key_terms.ٱلْخِتَانَانِ: the two circumcised parts, referring to sexual contact through penetration
key_terms.ٱلْغُسْلُ: ritual bath made obligatory after certain states of major ritual impurity
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءُ مِنَ ٱلْمَاءِ: the statement that water is only due from water, meaning ghusl only upon ejaculation

ai.seo_question: Does ghusl become obligatory after intercourse even if no ejaculation occurs?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of janabah when intercourse occurs without ejaculation. It reports that Imam 'Ali عليه السلام affirmed that mere meeting of the circumcised parts makes ghusl obligatory, and this view was accepted in the discussion.
